text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London finished firmer in thin activity. August added 50 cents to close at $323.50 per tonne, while October added 70 cents to close at $318.20 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York settled barely higher in thin trade. July closed 1 point higher at 11.37 cents/lb, while October added 2 points to close at 11.33 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 1 and 2 points. Prices were firmer than had been expected as speculators are apparently taking their time rolling out of July and into October. The July contract expires on June 30 and open interest in the spot month remains high. As of June 19, open interest stood at 47,914 lots.

JAPAN - According to the Agriculture Ministry, sugar production in 1996/97 (October/September) fell to 778,000 tonnes, raw value, down from nearly 900,000 tonnes the previous year and 821,000 tonnes produced in 1994/95. Typhoons, drought and cold weather were blamed for the lower production. This, however, is not thought to have any impact on imports due to gradually falling sugar consumption.

EUROPEAN UNION - Sugar production in 1997/98 is forecast to fall by about 650,000 tonnes, white value, Commission sources said. Last year's production was put at 16.5 million tonnes. It was added that although the area sown to beet is 1 per cent higher than the 2.02 million ha sown in 1996/97, the average sugar yield is expected to fall to 7.78 tonnes per ha, from 8.18 tonnes in 1996/97. It was added that lower yields reflect dry weather conditions in Northern Europe earlier this year. A quota production is expected to rise by 60,000 tonnes, mainly due to increases in Portugal and Greece. B sugar production is also expected to be slightly higher. Hence, the fall will be entirely in C sugar, it was added. The C sugar carryover into 1998/99 is tentatively put at 1 million tonnes against 970,000 tonnes the previous season.

SWAZILAND - Swaziland exported 246,298 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in May/February 1996/97, 20 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995/96. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 (May/April) dropped to 217,601 tonnes from 104,916 tonnes the previous year, due to lower production. Main export markets are the EU, the United States and Mozambique.
